name: source-reconfirmation-blind-spot
definition: practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS (line 29: severity, window, what, where) decide every REVISED event this observatory ever records; GDACS's own properties.datemodified is present in every preserved snapshot but is never read or compared. obs-2026-08-15-1.json found two GDACS drought futures that read identically in the registry -- both OPEN, both zero REVISED events since NOTARIZED on 2026-08-08, both apparently untouched for the observatory's entire six-night history -- whose raw datemodified diverges sharply: gdacs-dr-1017863 has a different datemodified on every one of the six recorded nights (2026-08-08T17:35:17 through 2026-08-15T05:55:20), while gdacs-dr-1018327's datemodified has read the identical 2026-05-21T13:07:09 in every preserved snapshot, three months before this observatory's first night. The current registry cannot tell these two facts apart -- 'the source re-examined this record today and confirmed nothing tracked changed' versus 'the source has not looked at this record in months' -- because it does not read the one field GDACS itself uses to say which is true.
test_rule: On each nightly run, for every OPEN GDACS-sourced future, read properties.datemodified from the night's preserved snapshot and record it alongside the future's registry entry in that night's run summary (a new field, e.g. source_datemodified, additive -- it does not feed TRACKED_FIELDS and does not generate REVISED events, since datemodified moving is not itself a claim that anything about the hazard changed). Compute days_since_datemodified_changed by comparing against the datemodified value recorded on this future's previous run (falling back to a scan of all preserved snapshots on the first night this sensor runs, since no prior recorded value exists yet). The sensor fires as a note the first time any OPEN, actively-fed future shows days_since_datemodified_changed >= 30 -- a round threshold chosen to sit well past the roughly daily cadence seen on the rolling class and well short of the three-month gap already observed for gdacs-dr-1018327, so the sensor would have fired on that case had it been running since this observatory's first night.
falsification: Falsified if datemodified turns out not to be a per-record signal after all -- e.g. if a wider sample across GDACS's other hazard types shows it moving in lockstep for large groups of unrelated events regardless of content, which would mean it reflects GDACS's feed-generation batching rather than the source's attention to a specific episode. obs-2026-08-15-1.json's spot check (gdacs-eq-1556215 stale at 2026-08-06 sitting beside gdacs-eq-1557236 fresh at 2026-08-15 in the same 2026-08-15 snapshot) argues against this for at least two non-drought events, but the sample is small and drawn from one night only. Also falsified in scope, not in kind, for NHC-sourced futures: nhc_futures() (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py) does not carry a comparable per-record modification timestamp in the current API response, so this sensor applies to GDACS-sourced futures only, the same scoping sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json already applies to a different GDACS-only field.
